IND vs NZ Tests: WTC hopes, Gambhir’s credibility on the line
 The manner in which India has approached this tour, from selection and a shadow tour to its preparations, made it evident that the two-Test series was the centrepiece of the tour
 Updated - November 16, 2026 05:35 pm IST - Wellington 
 Amol Karhadkar READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 India's head coach Gautam Gambhir. File
 | Photo Credit: PTI
 T20I series conquered with a hat-trick of wins at the start. ODI series was pocketed, with India clawing its way out of a hole in each of the three matches it won. For a majority of the fans, India’s tour of New Zealand would already qualify as a resounding success.
 But for the connoisseurs — and, more importantly, the touring Indian contingent — these have merely been the appetisers. The main course will be served over the next fortnight.
 IND vs NZ fifth ODI: Bowlers step up to lift India to 22-run win over NZ The manner in which India has approached this tour, from selection and a shadow tour to its preparations, made it evident that the two-Test series was the centrepiece of the tour.
 As the Indian contingent joined the other group, which had been training rigorously here for the past week, it was greeted by gusty winds. Wellington was so windy on Monday (November 16) that several flights were diverted or cancelled. Both teams, however, managed a safe landing from Tauranga.
 Captain Shubman Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir will hope the skies remain clear on Tuesday (November 17). After all, it will be the only full-fledged practice session that the entire 16-member squad gets together before the opening Test. With India having bolstered its pace resources by replacing Kuldeep Yadav with Gurnoor Brar as the sixth pace option, it will be interesting to see whether the lanky pacer, who walked away with the Player of the Series award in the ODIs, gets the nod ahead of Mohammed Siraj or Prasidh Krishna.
 Batting a worry as rookie pacers script rare triumph Getting the combination right will be crucial if India is to keep its slim hopes of qualifying for the World Test Championship (WTC) final alive. Placed fourth with seven Tests remaining — two in New Zealand followed by five in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy at home early next year — India needs to win the series or, at the very least, avoid defeat to remain in contention. Little wonder, then, that the tour has been planned with the clear objective of finishing on a high.
 Should India fail to avenge the 2024 home series whitewash against New Zealand, which triggered a prolonged downturn and hastened the transition in its Test set-up, the scrutiny of Gambhir’s credentials as Test coach is bound to intensify.
 Despite considerable success in multinational limited-overs tournaments, India’s Test returns under Gambhir have been underwhelming. Of the seven Test series comprising two or more matches that India has played since he took charge in July 2024, it has won three and lost three. The drawn series in England in 2025 remains arguably the high point of his tenure — a telling stat indeed.
 ‘They're a world-class outfit’: Matt Henry cautions against getting carried away after six-wicket haul against India The series victories have come against Bangladesh, the West Indies and Sri Lanka, none of whom have consistently challenged for a place in the WTC final. It is the defeats, though, that continue to rankle. The home whitewashes against New Zealand and South Africa, on either side of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy loss in Australia, have exposed India’s inability to find a settled combination and deliver consistently in the longest format.
 For Gambhir and his trusted lieutenants, the next fortnight is about more than winning another Test series. It is an opportunity to restore confidence in a team that has struggled to find its feet and, perhaps, silence some of the growing doubts surrounding its red-ball direction. The coach will hope to get it right come Thursday (November 19).
